title: Walking the Schrödinger Bridge: A Direct Trajectory for Text-to-3D Generation
motivation: SDS requires high CFG causing over-saturation and over-smoothing; existing variants still rely on noisy score matching
problem_framing: Learning optimal direct transport trajectory between current rendering distribution and desired target distribution
key_insight: SDS is mathematically equivalent to Schrödinger Bridge under Gaussian noise endpoint condition, enabling principled trajectory design
method_signature: TraCe constructs diffusion bridge from current rendering to predicted target, trains LoRA to learn bridge score dynamics
evaluation_criteria: CLIP Score, GPTEval3D, ImageReward, time, VRAM across 83 prompts
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Naive Schrödinger Bridge approach yields smoother, less detailed rendering compared to full TraCe
evidence_for_taste: naive approach to direct Schrödinger Bridge...results in a comparatively smoother, less detailed rendering
VSD and CSD exhibit less-desired generation (e.g., missing details)
This reliance on high CFG values is often problematic
These score estimates can be noisy and are not guaranteed to represent an optimal direction
thinking_moves: Prove SDS is special case of Schrödinger Bridge via Nelson duality
Construct explicit bridge from current rendering to dynamically estimated text-aligned target
Use t-annealing to progressively focus bridge interpolation toward target
Ablate both LoRA adaptation and scheduled t-sampling separately and together
